name: Tiger Trap
label: K
lede: Rose Melberg started Tiger Trap in Sacramento in 1992 and had it finished by January 1994. In between came one album that outsold anything K Records had released to that point.

eras.title: From Olympia to a Sacramento garage band
eras.text: Melberg hears the K scene in person at a 1991 festival in Olympia, goes home to Sacramento and builds a band around her high school friend Angela Loy. A split single is out within weeks.

years.src: KEXP: Throwaway Style · Wikipedia: Rose Melberg
years.h: Rose Melberg goes to Olympia for the K Records festival
years.p: The 1991 International Pop Underground Convention is where she decides she wants a band of her own. She has just finished high school.
years.xp:
KEXP's Softies feature says Melberg traveled from Sacramento to Olympia in summer 1991 and played for the first time at the convention's Girl Night showcase, nerves barely contained. Wikipedia dates her appearance to August 1991.

Tiger Trap formed after she got home.

years.cap: Tiger Trap on a couch: Rose Melberg, Angela Loy, Jen Braun and Heather Dunn
years.src: Wikipedia: Tiger Trap · Trouser Press · KEXP: Throwaway Style
years.h: Melberg and Loy add a bassist from Tower Records
years.p: [[Rose Melberg|1206e9c0-a650-4e2d-bd7c-6bc1ae260634]] and her high school friend [[Angela Loy|338fccc6-cd04-470f-962a-78d36d4e7bc5]] bring in bassist Jen Braun, then drummer Heather Dunn. Melberg and Braun both worked at Tower Records.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Braun was recruited through the Tower Records job and Dunn through a mutual recommendation. Trouser Press has the band forming at a Flaming Lips show.

The name is disputed. Trouser Press says it came from a Beat Happening song. KEXP says it came from a Calvin and Hobbes strip, and calls the Beat Happening story a common mistake.

years.cap: Flyer for Green Day, Threadmill, Jumpstart and Tiger Trap, July 25, 1992
years.h: Bratmobile takes the other side of Tiger Trap's first record
years.p: The split on the Four Letter Words label has Tiger Trap's "Words and Smiles" on one side and Olympia's Bratmobile on the other. It is out within weeks of the band forming.
years.xp: KEXP singles out "Words and Smiles" as a song that catches the rush of a crush. Wikipedia says the split appeared within weeks of the band's formation.

years.p: Wikipedia lists the Tiger Trap single for K as 1992. The song comes back on the album as "Super Crush".

eras.title: Calvin Johnson, Seattle and a best seller
eras.text: Calvin Johnson takes the band to Seattle for a record that becomes K's best seller. A five-song EP follows, and the last show comes that December.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tiger Trap (album) · KEXP: Throwaway Style · KCSB: Tape Quarantine
years.h: Calvin Johnson produces the debut at Avast! in Seattle
years.p: Tiger Trap runs twelve songs in about thirty minutes. [[Heather Lewis|6857ba96-db87-4daa-b048-527f79e48f53]] of [[Beat Happening|449e44cb-bcae-4c48-a1af-5d8df0f81456]] did the cover, and [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] ran the sessions.
years.xp:
The opener is "Puzzle Pieces". Others include "You're Sleeping", "Eight Wheels", "Chester" and "Prettiest Boy". KCSB called it a record whose stakes are to dance and nothing more.

NPR's Maria Sherman heard sugar-sweet punk closer to Talulah Gosh than to the riot grrrl bands around it. Spin praised the melodies, and the Chicago Tribune the three-part harmonies.

years.cap: Ticket for Fugazi and Tiger Trap, May 2, 1993
years.src: Wikipedia: Tiger Trap (album) · Wikipedia: Tiger Trap
years.h: Tiger Trap outsells everything on K until Beck
years.p: Wikipedia's album page says it was K's best-selling release until Beck's One Foot in the Grave arrived in 1994. The band page puts sales at about 10,000.
years.xp: The 10,000 figure comes from one source, Wikipedia. The band behind it had existed for roughly a year.

years.h: A five-song EP, Sour Grass, is the last record
years.p: Trouser Press lists it as the final Tiger Trap release, on K.

years.cap: Flyer for Idaho, Tiger Trap, Mary Lou Lord and Rocketship, Oct 22, 1993
years.h: Tiger Trap plays its last show at Bottom of the Hill
years.p: Wikipedia puts the final concert in San Francisco in December 1993, about a year after the band formed.

eras.title: A bad breakup, then the Softies
eras.text: The split was not friendly. A fan at a Sacramento show becomes Melberg's next bandmate.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Softies · KEXP: Throwaway Style
years.h: Tiger Trap splits, and not on good terms
years.p: Wikipedia's Softies page dates the split to January 1994, and KEXP says the band broke up acrimoniously.
years.xp:
Melberg told KEXP the band got a lot of attention quickly and "we were not really prepared" for it. She described the ending as the product of youth and not being able to support each other emotionally.

No source we found gives the specific reasons, so this page does not either.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Softies · KEXP: Throwaway Style · Trouser Press · Wikipedia: Tiger Trap
years.h: A fan at a Sacramento show becomes Melberg's next bandmate
years.p: [[Jen Sbragia|fa10b28a-aa6c-4991-a8aa-12d60746cc29]] met Melberg at a Tiger Trap show and got in touch after the band ended. The duo, [[The Softies|3daebde2-4630-40d8-be75-438edea4b281]], put out a K single, "He'll Never Have To Know", and the LP It's Love, both in 1995.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Calvin Johnson as producer of the single. Melberg told KEXP that Sbragia "really seemed like she was zoning in on me" at the show. The pair later moved to Portland.

Melberg also went on to Go Sailor and Gaze, where she played drums. Heather Dunn drummed for Lois, the reformed Raincoats and Dub Narcotic Sound System.

eras.title: Still the one people start with
eras.text: A band that lasted about a year stays in print and in conversation. Writers keep pointing new listeners at the album.

years.h: Pitchfork's "Twee as Fuck" essay sends readers to Tiger Trap
years.p: Wikipedia's album page cites the 2005 Pitchfork piece as highly recommending the record.

years.big: "a pioneering indie-pop outfit of four women"
years.src: Wikipedia: Tiger Trap (album) · Wikipedia: Tiger Trap
years.h: The A.V. Club calls it a possible gateway to twee
years.p: Rob Sheffield on the band, as quoted on Wikipedia. By 2014 The A.V. Club was steering new listeners to the album as an entry point.
years.xp: Wikipedia's album page also notes Complex ranking Tiger Trap No. 40 among the 50 best indie rock albums of the 1990s.
